stories-32-7-9-clay-despicable-fluid-and.title: First Human from Clay, Progeny from Fluid, and Threefold Endowment
stories-32-7-9-clay-despicable-fluid-and.note: Surah 32:7–9 distinguishes creating the first human from clay, his progeny from 'despicable water' (ma' mahin), and God breathing His spirit to grant hearing, sight, and hearts, matching Pirkei Avot 3:1 ('putrid drop') and Talmud Niddah 31a.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 32:7–9 separates Adam's original formation from clay from the reproduction of his descendants through seminal fluid, followed by the ensoulment of the fetus and the gift of sensory faculties.
discussion.reply: Genesis 2:7 describes Adam's formation from dust and the breath of life, while Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:1 coins the moral maxim that every human comes from a 'putrid drop' (tippah seruchah), rendered in Arabic as ma' mahin. Talmud Bavli Niddah 31a further assigns spirit, sight of the eye, hearing of the ear, and understanding of the heart specifically to God's contribution.

stories-32-7-9-clay-despicable-fluid-and.quranEn: [7] who made well everything He created. He brought about the creation of the human from clay, [8] then He made his progeny from an extract of despicable water, [9] then He fashioned him and breathed into him some of His spirit, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts. Little thanks you show!
quranHighlights: He brought about the creation of the human from clay
then He made his progeny from an extract of despicable water
breathed into him some of His spirit, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts

sources.title: Mishnah Pirkei Avot
sources.en: From where do you come? From a putrid drop. Where are you going? To a place of dust, of worm and of maggot. Before whom you are destined to give an account and reckoning? Before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.
highlights: From where do you come? From a putrid drop.
To a place of dust, of worm and of maggot.
sources.orig: עֲקַבְיָא בֶן מַהֲלַלְאֵל אוֹמֵר, הִסְתַּכֵּל בִּשְׁלשָׁה דְבָרִים וְאִי אַתָּה בָא לִידֵי עֲבֵרָה. דַּע מֵאַיִן בָּאתָ, וּלְאָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, וְלִפְנֵי מִי אַתָּה עָתִיד לִתֵּן דִּין וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן. מֵאַיִן בָּאתָ, מִטִּפָּה סְרוּחָה, וּלְאָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, לִמְקוֹם עָפָר רִמָּה וְתוֹלֵעָה. וְלִפְנֵי מִי אַתָּה עָתִיד לִתֵּן דִּין וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן, לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:

sources.title: Talmud Bavli, Tractate Niddah
sources.en: The Sages taught: There are three partners in the creation of a person: The Holy One, Blessed be He, and his father, and his mother. His father emits the white seed, from which the following body parts are formed: The bones, the sinews, the nails, the brain that is in its head, and the white of the eye. His mother emits red seed, from which are formed the skin, the flesh, the hair, and the black of the eye. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, inserts into him a spirit, a soul, his countenance [ukelaster], eyesight, hearing of the ear, the capability of speech of the mouth, the capability of walking with the legs, understanding, and wisdom.
highlights: There are three partners in the creation of a person
And the Holy One, Blessed be He, inserts into him a spirit, a soul
sources.orig: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה שׁוּתָּפִין יֵשׁ בָּאָדָם — הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְאָבִיו, וְאִמּוֹ. אָבִיו מַזְרִיעַ הַלּוֹבֶן, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ עֲצָמוֹת, וְגִידִים, וְצִפׇּרְנַיִם, וּמוֹחַ שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁוֹ, וְלוֹבֶן שֶׁבָּעַיִן. אִמּוֹ מַזְרַעַת אוֹדֶם, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ עוֹר, וּבָשָׂר, וּשְׂעָרוֹת, וְשָׁחוֹר שֶׁבָּעַיִן. וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן בּוֹ רוּחַ, וּנְשָׁמָה, וּקְלַסְתֵּר פָּנִים, וּרְאִיַּית הָעַיִן, וּשְׁמִיעַת הָאוֹזֶן, וְדִבּוּר פֶּה, וְהִלּוּךְ רַגְלַיִם, וּבִינָה, וְהַשְׂכֵּל.

phrases-32-5-day-whose-measure-is-a-thou.title: 'In a Day, the Measure of Which Is a Thousand Years of What You Count'
phrases-32-5-day-whose-measure-is-a-thou.note: Surah 32:5 declares that the cosmic affair ascends to God 'in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count,' matching Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4), 2 Peter 3:8 ('with the Lord one day is like a thousand years'), and Jubilees 4:30.

discussion.view: Commentators interpret the thousand-year day of Surah 32:5 either as the span of cosmic administration or as the length of a day in the Hereafter.
discussion.reply: The formula equating one divine day with a thousand human years is an established Second Temple and New Testament exegetical tradition rooted in Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4) and formulated explicitly in Jubilees 4:30 ('one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens') and 2 Peter 3:8.

phrases-32-5-day-whose-measure-is-a-thou.quranEn: He directs the (whole) affair from the sky to the earth; then it will go up to Him in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count.
quranHighlights: in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count.

sources.title: Psalms (Septuagint LXX)
sources.en: For a thousand years in your sight are as the yesterday which is past, and as a watch in the night.
highlights: For a thousand years in your sight are as the yesterday which is past

sources.title: Second Epistle of Peter (NASB)
sources.en: But do not let this one [fact] escape your notice, beloved, that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
highlights: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.

sources.title: Book of Jubilees
sources.en: And he lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens and therefore was it written concerning the tree of knowledge: "On the day that ye eat thereof ye will die."
highlights: for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens
